study_name.evidence_quote: study subjects were recruited among participants in a larger study in which Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg traveling for international exchange studies
study_name.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
study_name.notes: No explicit study name provided; inferred from description of Swedish exchange student recruitment.

target_condition.evidence_quote: The study population of travelers was exposed to a variety of health care settings at each travel destination and environments where the prevalence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria is especially high
target_condition.notes: Study investigates dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes via travel; primary focuses are on ESBL-producing bacteria and broad resistance gene abundance.

control.evidence_quote: Only health care students (medical, nursing, and dentistry) traveling to the Indian peninsula or to Central Africa and having submitted a full set of fecal specimens qualified for inclusion
control.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
control.notes: Study is observational, tracking students before and after travel; no traditional control group is used. Classification as 'Not Used' reflects that samples are paired longitudinal measurements within individuals.

country.evidence_quote: Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg traveling for international exchange studies
country.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
country.notes: Country of residence; students traveled to Indian peninsula or Central Africa.

body_site.evidence_quote: self-submission of separate fecal specimens for metagenomic analysis and culture screening
body_site.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection

days_from_first_collection.evidence_quote: The fecal specimens were collected at a median of 4 days before departure (range 0 to 23) and 22 days (range 2 to 120) after return to Sweden.
days_from_first_collection.notes: Study involves paired sampling: before travel (median 4 days pre-departure) and after travel (median 22 days post-return). Cannot assign single days_from_first_collection value per sample; granularity indicates sample_level but timing varies.

location.evidence_quote: health care students traveling to the Indian peninsula or to Central Africa

value: Study population: 35 Swedish students, ages 23-34 years, 74% female (26/35)
Travel destinations: Indian peninsula (n=18) and Central Africa (n=17)
Median days before departure for pre-travel sample: 4 days (range 0-23)
Median days after return for post-travel sample: 22 days (range 2-120)
Two-thirds (23/35) participated in hospital-based patient work
69% (12/17 Africa, 12/18 India) had traveler's diarrhea (median 4 days)
No subjects took antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling
All travelers to Central Africa and 44% (8/18) to India used antimalarial chemoprophylaxis
Sequencing technology: Illumina HiSeq 2000 (metagenomic); Illumina MiSeq (isolate genomes)
178 different resistance gene types detected across all specimens
23 resistance genes found in all libraries; 35 genes in ≥90% of libraries
Integrases and ISCR elements significantly increased after travel
9 of 12 CTX-M-15 genes found on sequences identical/similar to known plasmid sequences
